chapter: New York bands and the first records
title: Decca afraid to record without drums or piano; 'Gramercy Square'
summary: Eddie Sauter wrote 'Gramercy Square', but Decca feared a band with no drums or piano.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And about that time oh, MCA said to me, asked me if I'd like to go into the Commodore with a bigger band. Now one of the records we made on Decca was 'Gramercy Square,' which was the first one that Eddie Sauter made.
He made a little arrangement for that, group and played mellophone himself. He had four horns. But --
But de -- Decca was afraid to record without a drum or piano. They just were scared of it, they didn't know what to do with just bass or guitar.
They didn't know how to make that --
Afraid it would be too thin.
Yeah, it would be too thin --
Of course, I think nowadays, they'd do it. I'd do it. But I think it was just habit, more or less --
-- that made them think that they can't do it that way.
